findings.key: R1|user|alice@contoso.example|Privileged user can register a synced passkey
findings.title: Privileged user can register a synced passkey
findings.subject: alice@contoso.example
findings.detail: alice@contoso.example (Global Administrator) can register: Synced passkey, any provider, unattested. Their stricter admin profile is overridden.
evidence: alice@contoso.example holds privileged role(s): Global Administrator
All users (tenant-wide target) → scoped to profile 'Default'
member of group 'Privileged Admins' → scoped to profile 'Admins - device-bound'
Profile 'Default': deviceBound + synced; no attestation; no AAGUID restriction
Profile 'Admins - device-bound': deviceBound; attestation required; allow-list of 3 AAGUID(s)
Microsoft rule: a passkey is allowed if it satisfies at least one scoped profile; there is no most-restrictive-wins.
Effective weakest credential: Synced passkey, any provider, unattested (permitted by 'Default')
The stricter profile(s) 'Admins - device-bound' never get a say for this credential.
findings.action: Exclude privileged users from the target(s) 'All users' of the loose profile (e.g. scope it to a group that excludes admins), and scope admins only to a device-bound, attested profile.

findings.key: R6|profile|Admins - device-bound|Attested profile is bypassed by an overlapping profile
findings.title: Attested profile is bypassed by an overlapping profile
findings.subject: Admins - device-bound
findings.detail: 3 of 3 users scoped to attested profile 'Admins - device-bound' can still register unattested passkeys through another profile.
evidence: Users affected: alice@contoso.example, bob@contoso.example, carol@contoso.example
Union semantics: the attested profile only constrains users who have no looser profile.
findings.action: Remove the users of 'Admins - device-bound' from the targets of looser profiles, or accept that 'Admins - device-bound' is not an attestation control for them.

R1.name: Overlap weakening
R1.definition: A privileged user can register a weaker passkey than the admin profile intends, because at least one scoped profile allows it.

R2.name: Weak key already held
R2.definition: A privileged user already holds a synced or unattested passkey.

R3.name: Deadline cohort
R3.definition: User's only MFA is SMS or voice. They hit a blocking passkey registration prompt on 1 Feb 2027 (Global Admins and external users: 1 Jul 2027).

R4.name: Auto-enabled admin
R4.definition: A privileged SMS/voice user sits in an 'all passkey types' profile, the shape Microsoft auto-enabled on 1 Sep 2026.

R5.name: AAGUID trap
R5.definition: A user holds a passkey that none of their scoped profiles accepts. Microsoft blocks keys whose AAGUID is not permitted, so they lose sign-in with it.

R6.name: Attestation illusion
R6.definition: A profile is relied on as 'attested' but synced passkeys cannot be attested, or its users can bypass it through another profile.

R7.name: No phishing-resistant method
R7.definition: A privileged user has no phishing-resistant method registered.

R8.name: Campaign gap
R8.definition: The registration campaign will not reliably move the SMS/voice cohort to passkeys before the deadline.

R9.name: Excluded but privileged
R9.definition: A privileged user is excluded from the passkey policy. Exclusion beats every inclusion, so they cannot use passkeys at all.

R10.name: Policy hygiene
R10.definition: Profile count, list size, unused or dangling references, and auto-added Authenticator AAGUIDs.

notes: Per-user FIDO2 detail is exported for privileged users and the SMS/voice cohort only, which keeps Graph calls bounded. Rules that read registered keys (R2, R5) cover that scope.
